headline: Revenue and volumes ramp sharply, but GAAP loss persists
summary_short: MP's Q1 2026 revenue rose 49.1% y/y to $90.6M on a 117% jump in NdPr sales volume and $42.3M of DoW price-protection income, while the company remained at a GAAP net loss of $8.0M (-$0.04 diluted EPS), narrower than the $22.6M loss a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by higher NdPr oxide/metal sales volumes and prices plus new magnetic-precursor sales to GM, partly offset by the July 2025 exit from Chinese concentrate sales. Materials Segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 877% y/y to $36.7M on the volume ramp and $42.3M of DoW price-protection income; Magnetics Segment Adjusted EBITDA reached $9.6M. Higher cost of sales, SG&A, start-up costs and an $8.8M litigation settlement kept the company at a GAAP net loss, though it narrowed y/y. Operating cash usage improved $61.3M on higher sales and $51.0M of DoW PPA cash received. Capex rose to $77.4M on HREE, Independence and 10X Facility construction; management guides to $500-600M FY2026 capex. Cash fell to $886.3M q/q on investment purchases and capex.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and Segment Adjusted EBITDA both grew sharply on the NdPr production/sales ramp and DoW price-protection income, but higher opex, a litigation settlement and interest expense kept the company at a GAAP net loss.
Higher NdPr oxide/metal sales volumes and market prices, plus new magnetic-precursor sales, drove revenue up, partly offset by the July 2025 cessation of rare-earth-concentrate sales to China.
Net loss narrowed as higher revenue, PPA income and Segment Adjusted EBITDA more than offset higher interest expense, SG&A, start-up costs and an $8.8M litigation settlement.
Diluted EPS loss narrowed in line with the smaller net loss; diluted share count also rose about 8.7% y/y from prior equity issuance, adding a modest offsetting drag.
EBITDA improved on higher revenue and PPA income tied to the 117% y/y jump in NdPr Sales Volume, which drove Materials Segment Adjusted EBITDA up 877% y/y to $36.7M.
Operating loss narrowed as revenue and PPA income growth outpaced higher cost of sales, SG&A, start-up costs and the litigation settlement within other operating costs.
Cash usage fell $61.3M y/y, driven by higher product sales, $51.0M of DoW PPA cash received (none a year ago), and $19.0M from the 45X Credit on the 2024 tax return.
Capex rose $46.9M y/y from increased construction spend on the HREE separations facility, the Independence Facility expansion, and initial 10X Facility purchases.
Cash fell q/q as $259.8M of net investing outflows (mostly short-term investment purchases and capex) and $18.5M of financing outflows outweighed the modest $1.9M of operating cash usage.
Not explained as a standalone line in the release; the small q/q increase is roughly consistent with debt-discount amortization slightly exceeding scheduled principal payments.
Equity dipped slightly q/q on the $8.0M net loss and $17.6M of shares withheld for employee payroll-tax on vesting awards, mostly offset by $14.4M of stock-based compensation.
